subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the area of the parallelogram whose diagonals are 3i + j − 2k and i − 3j + 4k.

steps.label: Find d₁×d₂
steps.margin_note: First mark. Same cross-product step as before — but these are DIAGONALS, not sides, and that changes the formula at the end. Take the −2 out to keep the numbers small.
steps.memory_tip: These are DIAGONALS, not sides, and that changes the formula at the end. Take the −2 out.
lines: Given diagonals d₁ = 3i + j − 2k, d₂ = i − 3j + 4k

recall.must_convey: That the cross product of the two diagonals is computed, giving −2(i + 7j + 5k).
accept: cross the two diagonals to get minus two i minus fourteen j minus ten k, then take minus two out
take d one cross d two and factor out the minus two
the cross product of the diagonals is minus two into i plus seven j plus five k
diagonals cross cheste minus two common teeyyochu
compute the cross product of the diagonals

steps.why: Factoring the −2 out before the magnitude turns √(4 + 196 + 100) into 2√(1 + 49 + 25) — the same number with far smaller arithmetic.
common_mistakes: Treating the diagonals as if they were sides.
Sign slip on the j term.

steps.label: Halve the magnitude
steps.margin_note: Second mark, and the difference from the previous question. From DIAGONALS the area is HALF the magnitude — the half is not optional here.
steps.memory_tip: From DIAGONALS the area is HALF the magnitude — the half is not optional here.

recall.must_convey: That the area from diagonals is HALF the magnitude of their cross product, giving √75 = 5√3 square units.
accept: from diagonals the area is half the magnitude so it is root seventy five which is five root three
halve it because these are diagonals, giving five root three square units
the area is five root three square units
diagonals kabatti half teeskovali, five root three vasthundi
half of two root seventy five is root seventy five equals five root three

steps.why: The diagonals of a parallelogram span a figure twice its area, so the half corrects for that. Using the sides formula here would double the answer.

insider_note: The DIAGONALS are given, not the sides, so the area is HALF the cross product. Using the full magnitude doubles the answer; take the factor 2 out early to keep the surd simple.
